thread.title: Apple iPhone: Let’s Hope Average Prices Decline, Says RBC

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Apple iPhone: Let’s Hope Average Prices Decline, Says RBC
text:
Apple ’s ( AAPL ) average price for its iPhone may be going down with the next batch of models, presumably this fall, and that may not be a bad thing, writes RBC Capital analyst Amit Daryanani today.
Daryanani's note is among those that have focused on pricing since Apple's iPhone numbers last quarter turned up lower than the Street had been forecasting at the time, dashing hopes of a "super cycle" in iPhones.
Sifting through recent rumors, Daryanani comes up with pretty much everything you’ve heard already about what the line-up may be this fall. Two models used “ organic light-emitting diode ” technology, or OLED, just like the current iPhone X . One will be the same size as the current X, 5.8 inches on the screen’s diagonal, while another will be larger, 6.5 inches. And a third model will not use OLED but instead a plain-old LCD screen, measuring 6.1 inches on the diagonal.
The important thing is overall price will come down as Apple will likely sell the smaller OLED model for $100 cheaper than the X. The “XI,” as the analyst dubs it, may retail starting at $899. The larger model of OLED may assume the current X price, $999. And the LCD model “could be priced at $700."
“The most interesting dynamic to watch will be pricing,” writes Daryanani, “specially considering the limited success iPhone X had with $1,000+ ASP."
With lower overall pricing, Daryanani thinks the upside will come from the fact “it will drive stronger unit growth."
“Overall, we think the focus this cycle will be around Apple’s ability to segment market and expand its installed base,” writes Daryanani.
The payoff will be if Apple can lower its cost to manufacture the new devices, he concludes, supporting its gross profit margin:
GMs [gross profit margin] would benefit from cost downs from suppliers. Further, NAND pricing has been trending lower in CY18, which could provide another tailwind. Installed base growth even at low-end model provides services tailwind to GM. Our analysis suggests services gross margins (~60%) are ahead of corporate average and to the extent 18% services CAGR is achievable it should provide 50-60bps of GM tailwind.
Apple shares today rose $7.83, or almost 5%, to close at $172.77.
